protocol.purpose: M5 selector forced-COW matched-control throughput gate
protocol.candidate: Unmodified production selector and runtime from the frozen source revision.
protocol.control: The same source, compiler, build configuration, fixture and runtime with only selector-control.patch applied. MutableGuard is forced directly to FreshCow; Semantic selection remains unchanged so setup and semantic behavior stay valid.
protocol.bucket_scope: Resident CPU/CpuRam partial writes, H=0, one thread, one in-flight operation, diagnostics disabled. Current M5 has no handoff and therefore selects FreshCow for these PreserveContents MutableGuard writes.
protocol.metric: Direct completed-operation throughput reported by the fixture as completed_operations / wall_ns. This is not inferred by inverting sampled latency.
protocol.comparison: Per-pair candidate/control throughput ratio. The control changes only the selector result computation for the measured forced-COW intent; allocation, copy, publication, drain and fixture code are identical.
protocol.tolerance: Candidate throughput regression must not exceed 2% in either required bucket: candidate/control >= 0.98.
protocol.confidence: For two required buckets, each bucket uses a one-sided 97.5% paired-bootstrap lower bound, giving at least 95% familywise confidence by Bonferroni. The statistic is the median paired throughput ratio.
protocol.run_order: Rotate bucket order by pair. Alternate control/candidate order on successive pairs. Preserve all samples.
protocol.stop_rule: Exactly 20 independent process pairs per bucket; no optional stopping, sample deletion or rerun replacement.
protocol.environment: No build, TSAN, profiler or other benchmark runs concurrently. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen; KIS_CPU_BASELINE_LOOPS=4; KIS_CPU_BASELINE_RATE_MS=500; KIS_BR1_STAGE_PROFILE=0.
protocol.secondary_evidence: Preserve process wall time, setup, manager destruction, correctness and loader identity. These are reported but do not replace the selector throughput gate.
protocol.limits: This gate closes the M5 selector regression requirement only. It is not the full upstream CPU BR1-PERF, M/K/X/E matrix, tail-latency qualification or M6/M7 handoff performance.
